about.intro_content: Prof. Zhong-Jun Xia is a Professor in the Department of Hematological Oncology at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (SYSUCC), Guangzhou, with over 30 years of experience treating hematological malignancies.
about.detailed_content: Prof. Xia has led long-term follow-up studies demonstrating dramatic improvement in outcomes for newly diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma treated with rituximab plus CHOP at SYSUCC. He has served as Principal Investigator on clinical trials combining GELOX chemotherapy with radiation therapy for extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma, and his research has examined immune checkpoint biomarkers, including soluble PD-L1 and interleukin-2 receptor levels, as predictors of treatment response in multiple myeloma. He has published more than 170 research papers.

faq.section_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Prof. Zhong-Jun Xia

items.question: Does Prof. Zhong-Jun Xia accept international patients?
items.answer: CancerFax can coordinate medical report review and consultation support for international patients seeking an opinion related to lymphoma or multiple myeloma at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, subject to hospital availability and case acceptance.

items.question: What is Prof. Xia's area of specialisation?
items.answer: Prof. Xia specialises in the treatment of lymphoma, including diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma, as well as multiple myeloma.

items.question: How can I request a consultation or second opinion?
items.answer: Submit your medical reports through CancerFax. The CancerFax team reviews the documents, prepares the case for submission, and coordinates next steps with SYSUCC's International Medical Center, subject to availability.

items.question: Is Prof. Xia involved in clinical trials for lymphoma?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Xia serves as Principal Investigator on trials combining GELOX chemotherapy with radiation therapy for extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma.

items.question: Does Prof. Xia's team use biomarkers to guide myeloma treatment?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Xia's research has examined biomarkers such as soluble PD-L1 and interleukin-2 receptor levels as predictors of treatment response in multiple myeloma.
